methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description:
The dict describes another adapter type, or turns on a feature
v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

members.summary: What every adapter config holds, and the `adapter_config.json` round trip.
members.extended:
The base of each method's config (`LoraConfig`), with the fields
the reference's `PeftConfig` has.  Called on `PeftConfig` itself,
`from_pretrained` / `from_dict` read the method the file names and
return that method's config — the reference's idiom for learning which
base model an adapter needs before loading either.  It is not built
directly: a config of no method adapts nothing.

members.name: PeftType
members.signature: PeftType()
members.summary: The parameter-efficient method an adapter file holds.
members.extended:
The members are the reference library's `peft_type` strings, so a
config file names its method the same way on both sides.
`lucid.peft` implements every member: the LoRA family (`LORA`, `ADALORA`), the
orthogonal and LyCORIS families (`OFT`, `BOFT`, `HRA`, `LOHA`, `LOKR`), the shared-table
tuners (`VERA`, `VBLORA`, `RANDLORA`), the structured and sparse updates (`MISS`, its
predecessor `BONE`, `SHIRA`, `C3A`, `FOURIERFT`), `IA3`, `LN_TUNING`,
`TRAINABLE_TOKENS`, the prompt-learning methods (`PROMPT_TUNING`,
`MULTITASK_PROMPT_TUNING`, `PREFIX_TUNING`, `P_TUNING`, `CPT`), the adaption prompt
(`ADAPTION_PROMPT`) and the routing and mixing methods (`POLY`, `XLORA`).  A file that names
any other type raises `NotImplementedError`.

Prompt tuning, prefix tuning and p-tuning put learned vectors in front
of the input — as extra token embeddings, or as extra keys and values
of every attention layer.  The sizes they need are the base model's, so
everything but `num_virtual_tokens` can be left `None` and is read
off the model's `config` when the adapter is built.

members.name: TaskType
members.signature: TaskType()
members.summary: The task an adapter was trained for, as `adapter_config.json` records it.
members.extended:
It chooses the model class `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` and
`PeftModel.from_pretrained` return: `PeftModelForCausalLM` for
`CAUSAL_LM` and so on (`MODEL_TYPE_TO_PEFT_MODEL_MAPPING`), a plain
`PeftModel` for an adapter with no task.  A classification or
question-answering wrapper makes the model's head trainable when it
has one under the reference's conventional name (`classifier` /
`score`, `qa_outputs`).

members.name: get_peft_model
members.signature: get_peft_model(model: nn.Module, peft_config: PeftConfig, adapter_name: str = 'default')
members.summary: Adapt `model` with the method `peft_config` names and return it wrapped as a `lucid.peft.PeftModel`.
members.extended:
The model is changed in place: each module `peft_config` selects
becomes an adapter layer of that method (LoRA, (IA)^3, LoHa, LoKr) around the
original, and every parameter but the adapter's is frozen.  `peft_config`
is not changed — the wrapper keeps a copy — with two additions the reference makes too: a
`base_model_name_or_path` read from the model's `name_or_path`,
when it has one, and, for a classification or question-answering
`task_type`, the model's `classifier` / `score` / `qa_outputs`
head added to `modules_to_save` so that it trains.

The class returned follows `peft_config.task_type`:
`PeftModelForCausalLM` for `"CAUSAL_LM"`, `PeftModelForSeq2SeqLM`,
`PeftModelForSequenceClassification`, `PeftModelForTokenClassification`,
`PeftModelForQuestionAnswering` and `PeftModelForFeatureExtraction`
for theirs (`MODEL_TYPE_TO_PEFT_MODEL_MAPPING` is the table), and a
plain `PeftModel` when the config has no task.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description:
The model to adapt — any module; a zoo model keeps its
`generate` and heads through the wrapper.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description:
What to adapt and how — a `LoraConfig`, `IA3Config`, `LoHaConfig` or
`LoKrConfig`; its method picks the tuner.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in each of its tables (`lora_A`, `ia3_l` …).

returns.description: The adapted model.

raises.description: `peft_config` is not an adapter config.

No module matches `target_modules`, or a match is not an
`nn.Linear`.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(16, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 4))
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=4, lora_alpha=8, target_modules=["0", "2"]))
>>> peft.print_trainable_parameters()
trainable params: 208 || all params: 548 || trainable%: 37.9562
>>> peft(lucid.randn(2, 16)).shape
(2, 4)

members.summary: Hold `module` beside a trained copy per adapter; the active adapter's copy runs.
members.extended:
Building one changes nothing about `module` — the tuner builds them
while it is still planning, and a plan that fails must leave the model
as it was.  Which of the copies train is the tuner's freezing step.  It
answers the tuner's `_AdapterSlot` protocol, as a tuner layer does.

At most one adapter is active here: two copies of one module would have
no rule for whose weights the forward pass uses.  `active_adapter` is
the active adapter that has a copy, or `""` when none does, in which
case the original runs.

`get_peft_model(..., modules_to_save=[...])` puts one of these where each
named module was, so `isinstance(m, ModulesToSaveWrapper)` finds them in an
adapted model.  The module as the base model had it is `original_module`,
and the trained copies are in the `modules_to_save` dict, keyed by adapter.

parameters.name: module_to_save
parameters.description: The module trained in full (a classification head, an embedding).

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Key of the first copy in `modules_to_save`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, ModulesToSaveWrapper, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4), nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], modules_to_save=["1"])
>>> _ = get_peft_model(net, config)
>>> head = net[1]
>>> isinstance(head, ModulesToSaveWrapper), head.active_adapter
(True, 'default')
>>> head.get_base_layer() is head.original_module, list(head.modules_to_save)
(True, ['default'])

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description:
One adapter per row of the batch (the first dimension of the
inputs): row `i` is computed with `adapter_names[i]` alone,
`"__base__"` for the base model, all in one pass, so requests
for different adapters can share a batch.  The adapters in use
are ignored.  Inference only, for LoRA on `nn.Linear`,
`nn.Embedding` and convolution layers (and `modules_to_save`
modules).

parameters.description:
For multitask prompt tuning: the task of each row of the batch, `(batch,)`
integers in `[0, num_tasks)`, whose prompt is put in front of that row.

parameters.description: Keyword arguments of the model's `forward`.

returns.description: What the model's `forward` returns.

raises.description:
`adapter_names` is given in training mode, names an adapter
the model lacks, a row count other than the batch's, or the
model holds merged adapters or a DoRA adapter among those named;
`task_ids` is given to an adapter whose prompt is not made per task.

The method is not LoRA, or the model has an adapted layer a
mixed batch cannot route (attention, a raw parameter).

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4))
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, config, adapter_name="a")
>>> peft.add_adapter("b", config)
>>> _ = peft.eval()
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> mixed = peft(x, adapter_names=["a", "b", "__base__"])
>>> peft.set_adapter("b")
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(mixed[1], peft(x)[1], atol=1e-6))

methods.name: disable_adapter
methods.summary: Run the base model alone inside the `with` block.
methods.extended:
LoRA updates are skipped (a merged layer is unmerged on entry, and
stays unmerged after) and every `modules_to_save` module runs as
the original; the adapter comes back when the block exits, even on
an exception.  Blocks nest: the adapter stays off until the
outermost one exits.  Merging inside the block is refused.  A
compiled model follows the switch: the state it branches on is
part of its cache key.
examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4))
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 4)
>>> base_out = net(x)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                       init_lora_weights=False))
>>> with peft.disable_adapter():
...     bool((peft(x) == base_out).all().item())
True

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.signature: save_pretrained(save_directory: str | os.PathLike[str], safe_serialization: bool = True, selected_adapters: list[str] | None = None, path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

parameters.name: path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion
parameters.description:
For an adapter initialised with `"pissa"`, `"pissa_niter_<k>"`
or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`.

`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks, or
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` is given with
several adapters to write, for a method other than LoRA, for a
DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` holds no adapter.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

modules) and `vit` (`query` / `key` / `value` fused into
`qkv`, LoRA only).  `"auto"` converts when the model's type has
a converter and the file is in a layout it changes; `True` always
converts and refuses a type with none; `False` reads it as it is.

describes something lucid.peft does not implement.

>>> import tempfile
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model

...     _ = fresh.load_state_dict(base_state)

members.summary: A model with adapters, saved and loaded as the adapters alone.
members.extended:
Wraps the model in its method's tuner (`LoraModel` for a
`LoraConfig`), kept as `base_model` (the user's model is
`base_model.model`), so the
state dict reads `base_model.model....lora_A.default.weight` and the
adapter file `base_model.model....lora_A.weight`, the reference
library's layouts.  Calling it runs the wrapped model, and any public
name it lacks — `generate`, `config`, a head — is read from that
model, so code written for the bare model keeps working.

The model holds any number of adapters by name.  `add_adapter` and
`load_adapter` bring one in beside the others (frozen and inactive),
`set_adapter` switches which one the model computes with — and
trains — and `delete_adapter` drops one.  `save_pretrained` writes
them all, the `"default"` one at the directory itself and each other
in a sub-directory of its own name.

Usually made by `lucid.peft.get_peft_model`, or by
`from_pretrained` for a saved adapter.  Both pick the class from the
config's `task_type`: the wrappers (`PeftModelForCausalLM` and the
others, `MODEL_TYPE_TO_PEFT_MODEL_MAPPING`) are subclasses of this
one, each registered for its task by `class Wrapper(PeftModel,
task_type=TaskType.X)`; an adapter with no task, or a task no wrapper
is registered for, gets this class itself.

members.extended:
Each key is mapped back to where the tensor lives in memory (the
adapter name put back in) and copied into the existing parameter,
which keeps its dtype, device and identity.  Every key is checked
before anything is copied: one that lands nowhere, or a shape that
differs, raises with the model untouched — an adapter loaded into the
wrong model must not pass for a fresh one.  An adapter tensor the dict
does not supply is reported in a warning and keeps its value.

methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.

...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))

methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

methods.signature: save_pretrained(save_directory: str | os.PathLike[str], safe_serialization: bool = True, selected_adapters: list[str] | None = None, path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

parameters.name: path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion
parameters.description:
For an adapter initialised with `"pissa"`, `"pissa_niter_<k>"`
or `"olora"`, which rewrote the base weight: the directory
where `save_pretrained` wrote that adapter right after
initialisation, before any training.  The adapter is written
converted to a plain LoRA of twice the rank
($\Delta W = s(BA - B_0A_0)$, `init_lora_weights=True`),
which loads onto the original, unmodified base model and sits
beside other adapters.  It converts one adapter, so pass
`selected_adapters` if the model holds several; the directory
is only read.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`.

`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks, or
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` is given with
several adapters to write, for a method other than LoRA, for a
DoRA adapter, for `use_rslora` with a rank or alpha pattern,
or the directory's adapter does not match the trained one.
`path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` holds no adapter.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  The adapter is built without its
initialisation's effect on the base, so an adapter saved from a PiSSA
or OLoRA start loads onto the (rewritten) base it was trained beside
as it was trained, and a pristine base is left as it is.  If the
tensors do not fit the model, the injection is undone before the error
is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

members.extended:
`AutoPeftModel.from_pretrained(directory)` is for an adapter saved
with no `task_type` — a vision model's, for one, since there is no
image task — whose `adapter_config.json` carries an `auto_mapping`
naming the class of the base model.  An adapter with a task is loaded by
the class of its task (`AutoPeftModelForCausalLM` and the others).

the package it names.  Only packages on `import_allowlist`
(`["lucid.models"]` by default) are imported, and what is found there
must be a class with `from_pretrained` (else `TypeError`).

summary: `lucid.peft` — parameter-efficient fine-tuning: LoRA and 25 other adapter methods, with one API.
extended:
Fine-tuning a pretrained model end to end updates, stores and ships every
weight.  LoRA (Hu et al., 2021) freezes them and learns, beside each
chosen `nn.Linear`, a rank-$r$ update $s\,BA$ — on GPT-2
small's `c_attn` at $r = 8$, 294,912 parameters, 0.24 % of the
model — so a fine-tune is trained, saved and swapped as a few megabytes.

The API and the adapter file format are the reference adapter library's,
names and defaults included, so a script written for it reads the same
and an adapter directory moves between the two:

```python
from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model

config = LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=16, target_modules=["c_attn"],
                    task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
model = get_peft_model(base_model, config)    # base_model changed in place
model.print_trainable_parameters()
...                                            # train: only the adapter learns
model.save_pretrained("my-adapter")            # adapter_config.json + adapter_model.safetensors

PeftConfig.from_pretrained("my-adapter").base_model_name_or_path  # which base it needs
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh_base_model, "my-adapter")
merged = model.merge_and_unload()              # a plain model again, adapter folded in
```

Each method is a config class, a tuner and its layer classes, registered
by `PeftType` as they are defined (`lucid.peft.tuners._base`); the
entry points above dispatch on the method a config or a file names.  The
layer classes of each are in `lucid.peft.tuners.<method>`.  The methods,
by family:

* **LoRA family** — a low-rank update beside each frozen weight.  LoRA
  (`LoraConfig` / `LoraModel`) and AdaLoRA, which allocates the rank per
  layer during training (`AdaLoraConfig` / `AdaLoraModel`).
* **Orthogonal family** — a rotation of each layer's input space instead of
  an addition to its weight.  OFT (block-diagonal Cayley rotations,
  `OFTConfig` / `OFTModel`), BOFT (their butterfly factorisation plus a
  row scale, `BOFTConfig` / `BOFTModel`) and HRA (a chain of Householder
  reflections, `HRAConfig` / `HRAModel`).
* **LyCORIS family** — a weight-shaped update from a structured
  factorisation.  LoHa (a Hadamard product of low-rank products,
  `LoHaConfig` / `LoHaModel`) and LoKr (a Kronecker product,
  `LoKrConfig` / `LoKrModel`).
* **Shared-table tuners** — one set of tensors for the whole model, held once
  by the tuner, and a few parameters per layer.  VeRA (two vectors per layer
  over frozen random projections, `VeraConfig` / `VeraModel`), RandLoRA (a
  full-rank update from frozen random bases and learned scales,
  `RandLoraConfig` / `RandLoraModel`) and VB-LoRA (every low-rank factor
  mixed from one vector bank, `VBLoRAConfig` / `VBLoRAModel`).
* **Structured and sparse updates** — a weight update with a fixed structure
  other than low rank.  FourierFT (a few frequency-domain coefficients,
  `FourierFTConfig` / `FourierFTModel`), C3A (block-circulant blocks,
  `C3AConfig` / `C3AModel`), MiSS (one matrix shared across the shards of
  a weight, `MissConfig` / `MissModel`), Bone (the method MiSS replaced,
  kept to read old adapter files, `BoneConfig` / `BoneModel`) and SHiRA (a
  sparse subset of the weight itself, `ShiraConfig` / `ShiraModel`).
* **Scaling and selective tuning** — a small part of the model itself.
  (IA)^3 (a learned rescaling vector per layer, `IA3Config` /
  `IA3Model`), LN tuning (a trainable copy of each chosen normalisation
  layer, `LNTuningConfig` / `LNTuningModel`) and trainable tokens (a few
  rows of an embedding table, `TrainableTokensConfig` /
  `TrainableTokensModel`).

* **Routing and mixing** — several low-rank adapters combined per task or per token.
  Poly and Multi-Head Routing (every layer holds `n_skills` low-rank skills and a router
  with a logit vector per task, `PolyConfig` / `PolyModel`; the call names its tasks with
  `task_ids`) and X-LoRA (trained LoRA adapters loaded by name and weighed per token by a
  classifier on the final hidden states, `XLoraConfig` / `XLoraModel`; only the classifier
  is saved).
* **Adaption prompts** — LLaMA-Adapter: the top attention layers of a `gpt` / `gpt2` decoder
  attend to learned prompts through a gate that starts at zero (`AdaptionPromptConfig` /
  `AdaptionPromptModel`).

Everything below about adapters, switching, merging and files holds for all
of them (LN tuning applies, and merges, one adapter at a time; adaption prompts apply one at a
time; adaption prompts, Poly and X-LoRA cannot be merged into the weights).

**Prompt learning** is the last family.  It learns an input rather than a weight and adds no
layer to the model: prompt tuning (`PromptTuningConfig`: virtual-token embeddings in front of
the input), prefix tuning (`PrefixTuningConfig`: virtual keys and values in front of every
attention layer) and p-tuning (`PromptEncoderConfig`: the virtual tokens produced by an MLP or
LSTM).  The prompt is applied by hooks on the model's own call, so `model(...)` and the model's
`generate` both carry it; the adapter file holds the finished prompt as
`prompt_embeddings`.  They train one prompt at a time, have nothing to merge, and
support the causal-LM, sequence-to-sequence, sequence-classification, token-classification
and question-answering tasks (the last two get logits as long as the input, the prompt's rows
cut off at the head).  Multitask prompt tuning (`MultitaskPromptTuningConfig`) learns a shared
prompt and a low-rank factor pair per task, chosen per batch row by `task_ids`; context-aware
prompt tuning (`CPTConfig`) tunes a prompt of in-context examples with a bounded offset and
a loss over the examples' outputs:

```python
config = PromptTuningConfig(num_virtual_tokens=20, task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
model = get_peft_model(base_model, config)
```

What a LoRA layer guarantees:

* **The base is untouched until merged.**  The wrapped `nn.Linear` is
  kept as `base_layer` with its own `Parameter` objects — not
  copies — so an optimizer built earlier, a tied embedding and Core ML's
  identity-keyed weight sharing all still see them, and with the
  default initialisation ($B = 0$) the adapted model's output is
  the base model's, bit for bit.
* **Only the adapter trains.**  Every other parameter is frozen; the
  `bias` option and `modules_to_save` add biases and whole modules.
* **A half-precision base gets a float32 adapter**, computed in float32
  and cast back to the base's output dtype.
* **Merging refuses a shared weight.**  Folding the update into a weight
  another module also uses (a tied LM head) would change that module;
  `merge_and_unload` raises instead.

A model holds any number of adapters, each under its own name:

```python
model.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=4, target_modules=["c_attn"]))
model.set_adapter("style")                     # compute with — and train — this one
model.add_weighted_adapter(["default", "style"], [0.7, 0.3], "mix")
model.save_pretrained("adapters")              # "default" in adapters/, "style" in adapters/style/
model.load_adapter("adapters/style", "style-again")
```

The model class follows the task: `get_peft_model` returns a
`PeftModelForCausalLM` for `task_type="CAUSAL_LM"` (and the matching
`PeftModelFor...` class for the other tasks, which also train a
classification or question-answering head), and a config with no
`target_modules` takes the default for the base model's `model_type`.
An adapter directory that names its base model reopens in one call:

```python
model = AutoPeftModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("my-adapter")
```

LoRA layers exist for `nn.Linear`, `nn.Embedding`, `nn.Conv1d` /
`Conv2d` / `Conv3d`, their `nn.ConvTranspose` counterparts and
`nn.MultiheadAttention` (found by the module's
type in `target_modules`), and `target_parameters` adapts a raw
`nn.Parameter` of a module (`lucid.peft.tuners.lora`).  Asking for
more — `add_weighted_adapter` over anything but `nn.Linear` layers, an
adapter file of a method this package lacks — raises `NotImplementedError`
rather than doing less than asked.  Adapters are read from a local directory;
hub ids are not resolved.

`modules_to_save` trains whole modules (a classification head) beside the adapter; each
becomes a `ModulesToSaveWrapper` that keeps the original and a trained copy per adapter.  An
adapter written by the reference library for a model of the zoo is converted to the zoo's
module layout as it is loaded (`PeftModel.from_pretrained(..., convert=)`).  The reference
library and the zoo name some modules differently and lay a few out differently, so a
converter exists for each of these zoo model types (`model.config.model_type`):

* `"gpt2"` — the sequence-classification head `score` becomes `classifier`; no other
  name or tensor changes.
* `"roformer"` — the layouts agree, so a file converts by identity.
* `"t5"` — the reference's `block.N.layer.M.<Module>` nesting becomes the zoo's roles
  (`blocks.N.self_attention`, `cross_attention`, `feed_forward`, `<sub-layer>_norm`),
  and the text-to-text model's modules gain the `t5.` trunk prefix.
* `"vit"` — the separate `query` / `key` / `value` adapters are fused into the zoo's
  one `qkv` (exactly for LoRA; another method on those projections raises
  `NotImplementedError`), and the remaining modules are renamed.

`convert="auto"` (the default) converts when the model's type has a converter and the file is
in a layout it changes, and reads any other file as it is, such as one saved by
`save_pretrained`.  `True` always converts and raises `ValueError` for a model type with
no converter, or for a tensor the converter has no rule for.  `False` reads the file as it
is.  A model without a `config.model_type` is matched by the reference class that the
adapter's `auto_mapping` records.

A model can hold several adapters, switch between them, combine them
(`add_weighted_adapter`: `svd`, `cat`, `linear` and the TIES / DARE /
magnitude-prune types), and compute a batch whose rows each use a different
adapter (`model(x, adapter_names=[...])`).  `get_layer_status` and
`get_model_status` report what each adapter layer, and the model, is doing.
Adapting a model a second time adds the new adapter beside the first, with a
warning.
